description: Composite thermodynamic figure for the Fe–10Al–15Mn–0.8C–5Ni wt% low-density steel; all four panels are computed (Thermo-Calc-type) outputs. (a) Pseudo-binary phase diagram, temperature (°C, ticks 600–1400) versus wt.% C (ticks 0.0–1.6), with fields labelled L, L+δ, δ, δ+γ, γ, γ+κ and δ+γ+κ; a vertical dotted "alloy" line marks the alloy composition at 0.8 wt.% C, and red arrows label the "peritectic" reaction near ≈1.3 wt.% C/≈1290 °C and the "eutectoid" reaction near ≈1.05 wt.% C/≈850 °C. (b) Phase-fraction plot, temperature reversed 1200→750 °C, "vol. fra. phases" 0–0.8: black δ curve falls to zero, black γ-matrix curve rises to a maximum near 875 °C then declines, blue B2 appears abruptly at the "disorder-ordered trans., 1125 °C" dashed line, passes a minimum at the "eutectoid (851 °C)" dashed line, and green κ appears only below ≈900 °C at low fraction. (c) γ-matrix solute content (wt.% solutes) versus temperature: Mn ≈17, Al ≈8.3, Ni ≈3→1.5, C ≈1.4→0.8, with an "annealing" marker at 900 °C. (d) B2-phase solutes: Al and Ni rise to maxima near 850 °C, Mn decreases then recovers, C ≈0. Together the panels argue that δ→B2 ordering at 1125 °C plus Al/Ni/Mn enrichment into B2 drives the calculated microstructure.
measured_quantities: solute content in B2 phase (wt.% solutes)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a pseudo-binary phase diagram of temperature (°C) against wt.% C with the phase fields labelled L, L+δ, δ, δ+γ, γ, γ+κ and δ+γ+κ, and a vertical dotted line labelled 'alloy' at 0.8 wt.% C.

In panel (a) red arrows annotate the reactions labelled 'peritectic' (at ≈1.3 wt.% C, near 1290 °C) and 'eutectoid' (at ≈1.05 wt.% C, near 850 °C); no numeric temperatures are printed for these arrows.
In panel (b) the blue B2 curve appears abruptly at the dashed vertical line labelled 'disorder-ordered trans., 1125 °C', while the black δ curve drops steeply to zero at the same temperature.

In panel (b) the black γ-matrix curve reaches its maximum (just below 0.7 vol. fra.) at about 875 °C, close to the dashed line labelled 'eutectoid (851 °C)', and the γ-matrix volume fraction decreases on either side of that maximum.

In panel (b) the green κ curve is absent above ≈900 °C and rises only to a small volume fraction at the lowest temperatures plotted, matching the claim that γ→κ precipitation is limited in this system.

Panel (c) plots γ-matrix solute content (wt.%) versus temperature with Mn the highest at ≈17 wt.%, Al ≈8.3 wt.%, Ni decreasing from ≈3 to ≈1.5 wt.% and C from ≈1.4 to ≈0.8 wt.%; a vertical dashed line marks 'annealing' at 900 °C.

Panel (d) shows Al and Ni contents in the B2 phase rising with decreasing temperature to maxima around 850 °C (Al ≈14 wt.%, Ni ≈12.5 wt.%), while Mn first decreases to a minimum near 900 °C and then increases, and the C curve lies essentially on the zero line.

The caption states that the phase diagram demonstrates liquid (L), δ, γ and κ-carbide formation in the low-density steel system, and that panels (c,d) show equilibrium solute distributions with elemental partitioning from the γ-matrix to B2, consistent with Ref. [15] for the same alloy composition.
The caption states the phase-fraction plot (b) shows an order-disordered transition from δ to B2 at 1125 °C.
The citing text states that the eutectoid reaction occurs at 851 °C and that the δ-ferrite fraction is reduced on its way to B2 formation until that eutectoid reaction.

The citing text states that the extension of the eutectoid transformation near the annealing temperature of 900 °C enables fresh precipitation of B2 by reducing the γ phase fraction, and that γ to κ-carbide precipitation is limited in the system.
The citing text states that the thermodynamic calculations in Figure 1c,d show solute partitioning from γ enriching alloying elements into B2 through a local equilibrium at the phase interface.

The citing text states that solute partition into δ-ferrite from the γ-matrix during homogenization at 1150 °C for 2 h can transform δ to B2 via the order-disordered transition prevailing at 1125 °C in this alloy system.

The citing text states that B2 is enriched in Fe, Mn, Al and Ni, giving the chemical formula Fe(Ni, Mn)Al, and that the negligible solid solubility of carbon in B2 confirms the precipitated phase as an intermetallic.

sample_hints: alloy (0.8 wt.% C, marked in panel a)

subfigures.description: Pseudo-binary phase diagram, temperature (°C, 600–1400) vs wt.% C (0.0–1.6), showing L, L+δ, δ, δ+γ, γ, γ+κ, δ+γ+κ fields; a vertical dotted 'alloy' line at 0.8 wt.% C; red arrows annotate 'peritectic' and 'eutectoid'.

Phase volume fraction vs temperature (reversed axis 1200→750 °C): δ decreases to zero, γ-matrix peaks near 875 °C, B2 appears at the 'disorder-ordered trans., 1125 °C' dashed line and has a minimum at the 'eutectoid (851 °C)' dashed line, κ appears only below ≈900 °C.

γ-matrix solute content (wt.% solutes, 0–18) vs temperature: Mn ≈17 nearly flat, Al ≈8.3 slightly declining below 900 °C, Ni from ≈3 down to ≈1.5, C from ≈1.4 down to ≈0.8; vertical dashed 'annealing' marker at 900 °C.

B2-phase solute content (wt.% solutes, 0–18) vs temperature: Al (red) rises from ≈11.5 to a maximum ≈14 near 850 °C then decreases; Ni (blue) rises from ≈6.5 to ≈12.5 near 850 °C; Mn (black) falls from ≈13 to a minimum ≈10.5 near 900 °C then recovers; C stays ≈0. Dashed lines mark 'disorder-ordered trans. 1125 °C' and 'annealing'.
